statusReason: closed-partial, and the partial is now ONE named thing. Parcel 2's own predicate is MET and every item it owns is PASS: both products carry a deploy path that records the commit it built from against a tree proven clean, both products can report the commit they serve without holding a platform credential, both products carry a trigger whose home is a path, all three outcomes are observed over real HTTP in both products, the live refusal is recorded as a fact with its timestamp, and steps 1 and 2 are verifiably ONE commit per repo. parcels.parcel: STEP 1a -- the API records the commit it serves
parcels.evidence: scripts/deploy.mjs (new) resolves COMMIT = `git rev-parse HEAD` at deploy time and sets it TWICE on the Cloud Run revision: `--update-env-vars SERVED_COMMIT=<40-hex>` and `--update-labels commit-sha=<40-hex>`, from the same value. Both, because readApiSide() already reads both and refuses when they disagree, so setting one would leave the other rule unexercised in production. --update-not --set, because --set-env-vars replaces the whole env set and would silently delete plan-review's two plain env vars. Dry-run in both products prints the exact argv; live refusal names the revision and the missing field

parcels.parcel: STEP 1b -- the console records the commit it serves, without credentials
parcels.evidence: web/api/version.js (new, both products): a Vercel serverless function at /api/version, reachable because both web/vercel.json rewrites carry a negative lookahead excluding api/. Precedence SERVED_COMMIT then VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA. Refuses rather than defaults: 503 with commit:null, never '', never a branch name, never 'unknown'. Confirmed over real HTTP in the harness: 200 with the commit when set, 503 with commit:null when unset

The schedule is not decorative -- the mission's named bypass is 'a deploy made without running it', which only a schedule catches. Existence, cron and dispatch are asserted in both unit suites

completionPredicate: Done means: (a) both products carry a deploy path that resolves the commit from the tree the build actually came from, against a tree proven clean, and sets it on the API side as BOTH the env var and the label; (b) the console side reports the commit it serves, resolved rather than defaulted, so a check can read both sides WITHOUT a platform credential; (c) both products carry a trigger whose home is a path, naming what executes it, what triggers it, what fails and what bypasses it, with a schedule and not only a manual run; (d) all three outcomes are observed and filed for both products -- PASS with agreement (over real HTTP, not fixtures), FAIL on the recorded 2026-09-17 state, REFUSE with SERVED_COMMIT absent; (e) a live run is recorded with its timestamp and its refusal, as a fact and not an assumption; (f) steps (a) and (c) land in ONE commit per repo, verifiable from git; and (g) the three-question gate is answered in writing with the 'a human remembers' answer said out loud rather than implied away. All of (a)-(g) are met. The row's PRODUCTION predicate is met only after a deploy through the new path, which this lane may not perform.
theOneChangeAndWhyItWasKept: The mission states the one thing that can go wrong: arming a check that must refuse, before the deploy records a commit, fails every deploy of both products -- and an over-broad control is worse than a narrow one because it teaches the fleet to reach for the bypass flag. Kept by construction and verifiable: ONE commit per repo carries both halves (`git rev-list --count <parcel1head>..HEAD` = 1). And the first deploy through the new path cannot fail its own gate, because the gate runs AFTER both sides land and reads the SERVED surfaces, both of which report the commit that same change introduces. A real split still exhausts the bounded poll rather than being waited out, which is asserted in both suites.

threeQuestionGate.1_whatExecutesIt: scripts/served-commit-parity.mjs, in two modes: the default (platform records; needs the Vercel CLI) and --served (the two public origins; no credentials). Also wired into each product's `npm test`, and exercised end to end by scripts/g160-served-harness.mjs which runs in CI and on every scheduled run.
threeQuestionGate.2_whatTriggersIt: (a) DEPLOY-TIME -- scripts/deploy.mjs runs the check as its LAST step, after both sides land, with a bounded poll. (b) SCHEDULE -- .github/workflows/served-commit-parity.yml, cron every 2 hours plus workflow_dispatch.
threeQuestionGate.3_whatFails: A non-zero exit: 1 = the two sides serve different commits; 2 = a side could not be read. Either fails the scheduled job and blocks calling a deploy done.
threeQuestionGate.4_whatBypassesIt: (a) A deploy made BY HAND outside scripts/deploy.mjs skips the deploy-time gate -- the schedule is the control for exactly that case, and the honest limit is that it catches it within two hours, not at the moment it happens. (b) A deploy that passes SERVED_COMMIT from somewhere other than the commit it built -- caught as far as it can be, since the deploy refuses a dirty tree and the live surface of the SERVING revision must agree with the platform record. (c) --api-origin/--console-origin point the check at chosen origins; they exist so the harness can observe a real PASS without a deploy, they are measurement scoping and NOT a bypass, they cannot make two sides agree, and neither the deploy gate nor the schedule passes them. (d) 'A human remembers' is NOT an answer anywhere in this row: every trigger is a path or a job name.

whatIsLeftToTheIntegrationSeat: Push both branches and open the PRs. They are committed locally and unpushed; the lane does not publish.

Deploy both products through scripts/deploy.mjs (NOT by hand, and NOT with a deploy path that skips it) so that SERVED_COMMIT is recorded. This is the only step that can move the live verdict off REFUSED.

Expect the FIRST deploy through the new path to PASS its own gate. If it does not, the gate is over-broad and that is a defect in this parcel, not in the deploy -- the mission names this as the failure mode to avoid.

Expect a single post-deploy DISAGREE if the API deploys from HEAD while the console still serves the pre-deploy commit, and treat it as the gate working: the remedy is one console deploy from the same commit, which the gate will poll until it lands or until the bounded deadline expires.

The known strict case, already documented in Parcel 1's measurement: a commit whose tree is identical to its parent's (a merge) is a DIFFERENT COMMIT with IDENTICAL CONTENT, and a strict comparison reports DISAGREE. Left strict on purpose -- accepting a tree match would be a weaker rule than the row states, and this row was carded from a check that passed when it should have refused.
After the first live green run, the row's production predicate is met and its PLAN row can move. That verdict is the integration seat's to record, not this lane's.
